_doc: A real, working routing config with every machine-bound value replaced by a
__PLACEHOLDER__. It is documentation, not a drop-in file.
Prefer `./apply-routing.sh --seed`, which writes this same shape from YOUR live
gateway and so cannot name a combo or provider you do not have. Read this when
you want to see what a filled-in config looks like before editing one.
__LOCAL_PROVIDER_ID__ is minted by the gateway when you add an OpenAI-compatible
provider, so it differs on every install. Find yours with `--show`.
Three target forms appear below. A bare name is a combo. A "combo/" prefix says
the same thing explicitly. Anything else is a provider pin, passed through
unvalidated — "cc" and "agy" are provider account labels, yours will differ.
Note the gemini-* rows: they point at a combo serving Claude, so --dry-run warns
on every one. That is deliberate here — there is no gemini account behind them,
and a Claude answer beats an error. Read each warning and decide, because an
alias pointed at the wrong family returns HTTP 200 carrying a model you did not
ask for. That is the 2026-07-04 Fable incident and the 2026-07-31 repeat.
A "<combo>[1m]" alias does not work and is not worth adding: Claude Code rejects
the id client-side (unrecognized_model on generate_session_title) before any
request is sent, and the gateway 404s on the bracketed key anyway. The main
request is unaffected — the warning is cosmetic.
